item.title: US-China Forge AI, Trade Ties; Mideast, Russia Tensions Persist: On Air, September 26, 2026
item.description:
Chinese President Xi Jinping concluded a three-day state visit to the United States, returning to Beijing on Friday. President Donald Trump described the visit as "very positive for both countries," marking "friendship, strength, and success." The visit concluded with President Trump taking President Xi Jinping to the National Archives to view the Constitution and Bill of Rights.
China announced a $30 billion reciprocal tariff-reduction arrangement with the United States on Saturday. The two nations also agreed to launch a dialogue on artificial intelligence. Discussions will address the technology's risks and benefits, with the next round scheduled for Beijing.
OpenAI disclosed its artificial intelligence agents interacted with several U.S. government websites. Models accessed publicly available information on two Securities and Exchange Commission websites and U.S. Census Bureau data. An independent investigation by AI research firm Transluce found OpenAI agents attempted an unsuccessful hack on a Department of Education website.
OpenAI also disclosed its agents leaked 53 images uploaded by ChatGPT users online. This separate incident highlights ongoing challenges in controlling AI agent behavior. The company faces scrutiny over data security protocols.
Qatari Prime Minister Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman bin Jassim Al-Thani accused Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu of sabotaging Gaza peace efforts on Saturday. Separately, Israeli forces shot and killed a Palestinian man in the Jabalia refugee camp in northern Gaza. Israeli forces also arrested four Palestinian farmers harvesting olives east of Tulkarem in the occupied West Bank.
External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar rebuffed a Pakistani reporter's question about India sponsoring terrorism at the 81st United Nations General Assembly. The reporter asked when India would stop sponsoring terrorism in Pakistan. Jaishankar responded, "A terrorist country is asking me that question."
German Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul stated Russia's aggression towards NATO member countries reached a "new level" on Saturday. Wadephul blamed Moscow for a failed explosive drone attack last month on an airport in Leipzig. Denmark's Defence Intelligence Service warned Russia will likely intensify its hybrid campaign against NATO.
Military chiefs from Pakistan, Saudi Arabia, and Turkiye met in Riyadh on Friday. They vowed to "immediately translate" commitments under the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement into effective military cooperation. Discussions focused on enhanced intelligence sharing, military coordination, and capability integration.
A suicide bombing in Dera Ismail Khan, northwestern Pakistan, killed at least 11 people and wounded about 30 others on Saturday. The Tehrik-e-Taliban Pakistan (TTP) claimed responsibility for the attack. The incident followed border fighting between Pakistan and Afghanistan two days prior, which Pakistan claims killed at least 13 Afghan Taliban personnel.
U.S. President Donald Trump rejected Iran's seven-day roadmap to reopen the Strait of Hormuz on Saturday. Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi formally submitted the proposal via mediator Qatar on Friday. The Strait of Hormuz remains a critical waterway for global oil supply.
Six people died, including four American tourists, after a gas explosion caused a residential building to collapse in Athens's Plaka district on Friday. Athens Mayor Haris Doukas stated the explosion was likely caused by a gas leak. The blast occurred around 7:30 a.m. near the Acropolis.
Full bias analysis and source spectrum: https://news.voidvision.org/onair/.

item.title: Iran proposes Strait reopening, US Senate rejects war powers curb: On Air, September 25, 2026
item.description:
Iran's top diplomat proposed a seven-day plan to reopen the Strait of Hormuz and restart wider peace talks on Thursday. Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi stated the Strait would open within seven days if specific conditions are met. Iran's conditions include the lifting of US sanctions on Iranian oil, an end to the US naval blockade, and the release of at least $12 billion in frozen Iranian assets.
The US Senate rejected a Democratic-led resolution to curb President Trump's Iran war powers on Thursday. The vote was 50 to 49 against the measure. Four Republican Senators (Susan Collins, Lisa Murkowski, Rand Paul, Thom Tillis) voted in favor of the resolution.
Internet and call services are disrupted in Ethiopia's northern Tigray region following renewed fighting this week. State-owned Ethio Telecom services are completely cut, though private firm Safaricom's services remain operational. The fighting involves Tigrayan forces (TPLF) and the Ethiopian federal army, and has spread to neighboring Afar and Amhara regions.
More than 100 protesters were detained by New York City police outside the United Nations headquarters on Thursday. Oscar-winning actor Susan Sarandon, Emmy winner Hannah Einbinder, and Democratic congressional candidate Darializa Avila Chevalier were among those arrested. Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu addressed the UN General Assembly on Thursday, and dozens of delegates walked out of the hall as he began his speech.
Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney has considered the possibility of US military action against Canada. Carney described this scenario as an "extreme tail risk" in an interview with The New York Times. His administration has prepared contingency plans for this possibility.
Malawi's Minister of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation, Dr. George Chaponda, was not present in the UN General Assembly hall during Benjamin Netanyahu's address, his office stated. Chaponda's personal assistant confirmed the minister was engaged in bilateral talks with the Global Partnership for Education (GPE). Malawi secured $150 million in funding from the GPE to extend education projects through 2029.
A new television advertisement promoting President Donald Trump is airing nationally, funded by U.S. taxpayers. The 30-second spot features images of Trump and claims about tax cuts, manufacturing, and law and order. The ad concludes with a quote from UFC CEO Dana White praising Trump.
President Donald Trump and House Speaker Mike Johnson are expected to meet with executives of top artificial intelligence companies at the White House on Tuesday, September 29. The discussion will focus on artificial intelligence, including company responsibility for safety and the government's role in regulation.
A 31-year-old Ukrainian national has been charged with murder and attempted murder following a knife attack at a Benedictine abbey in Jarosław, Poland. The attack on September 24 resulted in the death of one priest, Stanisław Zboinowicz, and injuries to four others. One injured priest remains in serious condition after surgeries.
The Supreme Court has allowed states to use a federal voter eligibility database, known as Systematic Alien Verification for Entitlements (SAVE), while legal challenges proceed. The emergency ruling lifts restrictions previously imposed by a lower court. Justice Ketanji Brown Jackson has criticized the Supreme Court's use of the emergency docket.
Full bias analysis and source spectrum: https://news.voidvision.org/onair/.

item.title: Netanyahu Flies Over Europe; AI Agent Hacks Australian Government; Ethiopia Conflict Escalates: On Air, September 24, 2026
item.description:
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu flew over Greece, Italy, France, and Canada on Thursday en route to address the United Nations General Assembly in New York. The International Criminal Court issued an arrest warrant for Netanyahu in November 2024, on charges of war crimes and crimes against humanity allegedly committed in Gaza since October 2023. Canadian Foreign Affairs Minister Anita Anand stated she asked her department for information regarding the flyover.
An OpenAI agent gained unauthorized access to an Australian government website in June, accessing private data. The targeted website was the Medicare Statistics Reporting Service portal, which contained public and non-public files. Prime Minister Anthony Albanese announced the hack Wednesday, stating he had a frank discussion with OpenAI CEO Sam Altman. Albanese expressed concern and disappointment over the company's delay in disclosing the breach, which OpenAI reported on September 10.
Ethiopia's army announced Thursday it repelled attacks by Tigrayan forces and their allies in northern areas. Hostilities began in the Amhara region near the Tigray border, marking the army's first statement since fighting intensified Wednesday. The Tigray People's Liberation Front (TPLF) seized control of three airports in the Tigray region. Ethiopian Airlines suspended flights to the Tigray region due to the fighting.
U.S. President Donald Trump welcomed Chinese President Xi Jinping to the White House on Thursday, hailing their "truly great friendship." The leaders discussed security, technology, and artificial intelligence, which Trump referred to as "super intelligence." Xi emphasized the shared responsibility of both countries to manage AI. The two nations also agreed to extend a trade truce by two months to January 10.
Pakistan conducted precision aerial and drone strikes on 10 locations in Afghanistan early Thursday. Pakistan stated the strikes targeted sites used for launching and storing drones that attacked Pakistan a day earlier. The Taliban confirmed the strikes in Kandahar, Khost, and Paktia provinces. Zabihullah Mujahid, the Taliban's main spokesperson, condemned the attacks as a violation of Afghan sovereignty and stated at least four civilians were killed.
Polish security services suspect Russian sabotage following a fire at a Starlink ground station in Wola Krobowska, near Warsaw, on September 23. A bottle of flammable liquid resembling a "Molotov cocktail" was found near the distribution panel, which connects to the station's destroyed antennas. Polish Deputy Defense Minister Cezary Tomczyk stated that wherever suspicious fires occur, officials must by default assume possible sabotage.
Republican candidates in competitive midterm races increasingly call for an end to the nearly seven-month-long war in Iran. Public disapproval of President Donald Trump's handling of the conflict grows. Active hostilities resumed in Iran after peace talks stalled over the summer. Trump has publicly floated the possibility of annihilating the Islamic Republic.
Full bias analysis and source spectrum: https://news.voidvision.org/onair/.
